items.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
items.summary: An official Anthropic VS Code extension on Cursor was backdoored, reportedly threatening up to 5,000 developers' machines. The malicious version was distributed through the official Anthropic account on Cursor and involved a supply-chain compromise of the distribution channel. The extension was designed to install a persistent SSH backdoor, allowing attackers to collect host information and potentially steal cloud credentials. This backdoor attempted to establish a reverse SSH tunnel and beacon host details to an external server. Cursor and Anthropic have taken steps to mitigate the threat by removing the extension and shutting down the marketplace.

items.title: Pick a Number Between 1 and 10
items.summary: A viral chart comparing random number selection between humans, a random generator, and a large language model shows a peak at 7 for humans. This result is explained by gradient descent learning from human preferences, which favor the culturally loaded number 7. Post-training refinements and the decoding process further narrow the distribution, turning the human "hill" into a sharp "needle." The process involves understanding how models learn from human feedback and how sampling methods affect the final output. Ultimately, the LLM is not bad at randomness but is biased toward the most expected answer, 7.

items.summary: The winning insurance hackathon solution used supervised binning with the AutoCarver library to select and group features. Binning provided structure to messy insurance features, allowing a tree model to find patterns more effectively. While the final accuracy gains were small, the feature selection mechanism was key to the success. Subsequent audits showed that the performance gains were largely due to which features the selector kept, rather than the binning method itself.
